name: Transfer Pricing
title: Transfer Pricing
answer: Transfer pricing is the set of rules and methods that decide how prices are set for goods, services, loans and intellectual property moving between related companies in different tax jurisdictions. It sits inside corporate tax and jurisdictional compliance, and it matters most to multinational groups that file accounts in more than one country. The core question is always whether an intercompany price matches what unrelated parties would have agreed, the arm's length principle. Work in this area spans tax, finance, legal and operations teams rather than a single department.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Transfer pricing is the set of rules and methods that decide how prices are set for goods, services, loans and intellectual property moving between related companies in different tax jurisdictions. It sits inside corporate tax and jurisdictional compliance, and it matters most to multinational groups that file accounts in more than one country. The core question is always whether an intercompany price matches what unrelated parties would have agreed, the arm's length principle. Work in this area spans tax, finance, legal and operations teams rather than a single department.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Practitioners work from ledgers, intercompany agreements, segment reporting and country by country filings, usually held in ERP systems and tax reporting platforms. Benchmarking studies draw on commercial databases of comparable transactions and on public accounts. Documentation is assembled in spreadsheets, document management systems and dedicated transfer pricing software, and larger groups run master file, local file and country by country reporting packs across many entities. The site tracks 229 compliance and regulation pages, which reflects how much of this work is documentation and filing rather than analysis alone.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts with a functional analysis: who does what, who takes which risks, and who owns which assets inside the group. From there a method is selected, commonly the comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, transactional net margin or profit split approach, and tested against comparables. Economists and tax specialists run margin ranges, adjust for differences between the tested party and the comparables, and refresh the analysis as facts change. The output is a defensible position supported by contemporaneous documentation, ready for a revenue authority to examine.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Transfer pricing sits at the junction of tax law, accounting standards and treaty rules, and it is governed by each country's domestic legislation plus bilateral treaties and the OECD guidelines that most regimes follow. Risk shows up as audits, adjustments, penalties and double taxation when two countries disagree about the same transaction. Provenance matters because every number in a file must trace back to a contract, an invoice or a benchmark source, and mutual agreement procedures or advance pricing arrangements are the usual routes to resolving disputes. Nothing here is legal or tax advice, and readers should take their own position with qualified counsel.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more standardised documentation, more real time reporting and heavier use of data analytics to test margins continuously rather than once a year. Tax authorities are building their own comparables and risk scoring tools, which shifts the burden of proof toward taxpayers who can show their numbers clearly. Amount B style simplifications for baseline distribution and manufacturing activity are changing how routine returns are set. The site currently tracks 514 company pages and 401 merger and acquisition filings, and each new deal creates fresh intercompany flows that need pricing.
